extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, prosecutors, in-house counsel, and applicants dealing with Chinese (CNIPA) patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the China National Intellectual Property Administration's revised Patent Examination Guidelines (effective Jan 1, 2026), setting forth examination standards and procedural rules for patents, utility models, designs, reexamination/invalidation, PCT national phase matters, AI and bitstream inventions, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter requirements for inventor eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors stated in a patent application form must be natural persons and must qualify as true inventors who "have made creative contributions to the substantive features of the invention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor eligibility generally will not be examined during prosecution unless there is evidence indicating a listed inventor is not a true inventor. Emphasizes that inventorship requires creative contribution to substantive features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion of inventor information required in the application form
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification information must be provided for all inventors (not just the first inventor); for an initial period starting January 1, 2026 Chinese inventors must provide nationality and ID card number, foreign inventors nationality only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final revisions narrow agency obligations: patent agencies must verify authenticity of the applicant’s identification information and contact details but are not broadly responsible for accuracy of inventors' identification. CNIPA practice may evolve; monitor updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of practice regarding priority claims in divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a divisional application derived from a parent that claimed priority does not claim priority at filing, CNIPA will notify that priority is deemed not made; applicant may request restoration by paying restoration fee within two months of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes existing practice; priority restoration is generally permitted where parent claimed priority. The procedure clarified (notification + two-month restoration window).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of definition of "plant varieties" excluded from patent protection
rubrics_metrics.description: "Plant variety" defined as a group of plants artificially selected and bred or discovered and subsequently improved, exhibiting consistent morphological and biological characteristics and relatively stable genetic traits; naturally occurring wild plants discovered without technical processing are "scientific discoveries" and not patentable; wild plants that underwent artificial selection/breeding and acquired industrial applicability may be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns terminology with the Seed Law and Regulations on Protection of New Varieties of Plants; breeding intermediate materials and other plant-related subject matter that do not meet this definition may still be patentable. CNIPA provided additional illustrative examples in its Interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial revision of the same-day dual filing system for patents and utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files invention patent and utility model on same day but fails to declare reliance on the same-day dual filing system, applications handled under double-patenting refusal. Where declared, applicant must be notified to declare within time limit whether to abandon the utility model right; the patent cannot be granted unless the utility model right is abandoned; failure to respond leads to deemed withdrawal or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications registered on/after Jan 1, 2026 regardless of filing date. CNIPA intends to limit applicant flexibility and ensure the system is used consistent with initial policy objectives. Operational details remain to be observed in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step: disregard features not contributing to technical solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Features that do not contribute to the solution of a technical problem generally do not affect the assessment of inventive step of an invention, even if written into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should (1) challenge examiner's identified technical problem if inappropriate, (2) rely on specification disclosures or submit experimental data to rebut the examiner, and (3) ensure specifications clearly explain relationship between each technical feature and the technical effects achieved. Revision may increase rejections where applicants add non-contributing features to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of examination criteria and illustrative examples for AI-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded examination standards and illustrative examples for AI, big data, etc., including clarifications on scope (title change), examination principles, public order and morality, inventiveness, and implementability; follows approaches in CNIPA 2024 Trial Guidelines for AI-related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points included: (1) examine claims (and where necessary specifications); (2) new public_order_and_morality criteria under Article 5(1) — inventions that in data collection/tagging/recommendation/decision-making violate law, public order, morality, or harm public interest are not patentable; (3) illustrative morality examples (facial recognition for marketing; autonomous vehicle model using gender/age for collision choice) showing rejection; (4) added illustrative examples for inventive step in AI contexts (application-scenario-only differences usually lack inventiveness; substantive algorithm/model modifications that achieve technical effects may support inventiveness); (5) implementability/disclosure expectations for AI models (must describe necessary modules, model hierarchy/connections, training steps and parameters, integration with application domain, input/output data settings) to address “black box” concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria for inventions involving bitstreams
rubrics_metrics.description: New Section: claims directed merely to a simple bitstream, or where substantially all content other than the subject matter refers solely to a simple bitstream, are considered "rules and methods for intellectual activities" and not patentable; however, video encoding/decoding methods that generate a specific bitstream, storage/transmission methods for such bitstream, and computer-readable media storing programs to generate the bitstream may be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (1) for implementability, the specification must describe the specific encoding/decoding method clearly and completely so a skilled person can implement it; (2) claim drafting guidance: claims may be method, apparatus, and computer-readable storage medium claims and should generally be drafted referencing the specific video encoding method (examples of acceptable claim formats provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of the signatory for priority assignment documents upon PCT national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a PCT applicant obtained priority right by assignment etc., the documentary proof must be signed/sealed by all applicants of the priority application (change from previously "assignor").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision aligns wording with other parts of the Guidelines and does not change substantive procedures in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplification and omission of the composition of examination decisions in reexamination/invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination decisions shall "generally include" bibliographic data, legal basis, main points, brief of the case, grounds of decision, conclusion and drawings — granting adjudication panels greater discretion in drafting decisions; prior specific allowance to simplify/omit the brief of the case in certain decisions has been deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide drafting flexibility; not expected to produce significant substantive change but gives panels discretion to streamline decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing invalidation requests in another party's name / stricter invalidation requester qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: New ground for non-acceptance: the invalidation request is not made based on the true intention of the requester (targeting straw-man filings, forged signatures/powers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, CNIPA may require identity verification: requester appear in person with ID or submit notarized documents verifying requester’s identity and true intention. Failure to comply within 15 days may lead to deemed withdrawal. CNIPA signals stricter scrutiny of 'straw man' filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of scope of the "res judicata" principle for invalidation grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation requests based on not only grounds that are "the same" but also those that are "substantially the same" as grounds on which an examination decision has been rendered will not be accepted or examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two examples illustrate how later grounds may be "substantially the same" (support requirement variations; inventive-step/novelty overlaps). Aim: curb repetitive filings and conserve examination resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearer rules on amendments during invalidation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments are made during invalidation proceedings, the party must submit full replacement pages together with a comparison table showing the amendments; where multiple amended texts are submitted, only the last-submitted amended text prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies submission form and establishes that earlier amended texts in same proceeding will not be used as the basis for examination once superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional abolition of page-count surcharges for sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings submitted in the prescribed electronic data format shall not be counted toward the number of specification pages and shall not be subject to additional page-based filing fees; sequence listings submitted in paper form remain subject to original fee rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of official fees for PCT national phase updated accordingly (removal of prior 400-page counting provision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of rules on requests for refund of official fees
rubrics_metrics.description: In three specified situations where CNIPA previously could proactively refund fees, refunds will now be made only upon request by the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include: (1) substantive examination fee refund where app deemed/approved withdrawn before substantive examination stage; (2) annuity fees paid after decision terminating/invalidating patent in entirety; (3) restoration procedure initiated but rejected — refund of restoration request fee possible upon request. Parties must actively request refunds to receive them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit codification of expedited (prioritized/accelerated/deferred) examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon applicant's request, an application may be subject to prioritized examination, expedited examination, or deferred examination; applications passing preliminary exam at certain IP Protection Centers or Rapid Rights Protection Centers may be eligible for expedited examination if requirements met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally incorporates commonly used prioritized and accelerated examination practices for domestic Chinese applicants and clarifies eligibility routes for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of information shown on registration certificates for PCT applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications and their divisional applications, the "inventor(s)/designer(s)/applicant(s) at the time of filing" listed on registration certificates refer to those at the time the international application enters the Chinese national phase, or, for divisional applications, at the date of submission of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies snapshot timing for names on registration certificates in national phase/divisional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial revision of the calculation rules for Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods spent on reexamination will not be included in compensable patent term even if no amendments were made during reexamination and the prior rejection is overturned based on new grounds or evidence submitted by the requester after receiving the decision of refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that reexamination delays are not 'reasonable delays' eligible for PTA compensation where the overturn is based on new grounds/evidence submitted after refusal; aligns with implementing regulations' approach that certain reexamination-caused delays are not compensable.
